exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
Number of previous cesarean sections (single vs. repeated CS)
cohort: The study included 194 multiparous Caucasian women aged 18 to 40 years with a BMI ranging from 18 to 30.
finding: No significant statistical difference was observed in the three dimensions of the mons pubis between women who had vaginal deliveries and those who had cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Cesarean section, even when repeated, minimally affects the dimensions and ratios of the mons pubis.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at an unspecified time after delivery, comparing women with different delivery modes.
